scenes.title: Zeus Releases the Gods
scenes.summary: While the Achaeans arm around Achilles and the Trojans on the rise of the plain, Zeus bids Themis call the gods to assembly; every river comes but Oceanus, and every nymph. Poseidon asks why he has called them; Zeus answers that he cares for the men even as they perish. He will sit in a fold of Olympus and watch, and the others may go and help either side as they wish, for if Achilles fights alone the Trojans will not hold him even for a little while, and he may sack the wall against fate.

scenes.title: The Gods Go to War
scenes.summary: The gods go to war with their hearts divided: Hera, Athena, Poseidon, Hermes and Hephaestus to the ships; Ares, Apollo, Artemis, Leto, Xanthus and Aphrodite to the Trojans. While the gods keep apart the Achaeans exult and the Trojans tremble at the sight of Achilles; when they come into the throng, Strife rises, Athena shouts by the ditch and on the shore, and Ares from the height of the city and along the Simoeis. Zeus thunders, Poseidon shakes the earth and Ida, and Aidoneus leaps from his throne in fear that the earth will be broken open over the house of the dead. The gods stand paired: Apollo against Poseidon, Athena against Enyalius, Artemis against Hera, Hermes against Leto, and the river whom the gods call Xanthus and men Scamander against Hephaestus.

scenes.title: Apollo Sends Aeneas
scenes.summary: Achilles longs above all to meet Hector. Apollo, in the likeness of Priam's son Lycaon, asks Aeneas where his threats over the wine have gone; Aeneas answers that Achilles once put him to flight from Ida, when he came upon his cattle and sacked Lyrnessus and Pedasus, and that a god always stands at his side. Apollo answers that Aeneas too is the son of a goddess, and of a greater one, and breathes great might into him.

scenes.title: The Gods Sit Apart
scenes.summary: Hera asks Poseidon and Athena whether to turn Aeneas back or stand by Achilles, so that he may know that the best of the immortals love him; hereafter he will suffer whatever his fate spun for him at his birth. Poseidon will not drive the gods into strife: let them sit apart and leave the war to men, unless Ares or Apollo begin it. He leads them to the heaped-up wall that the Trojans and Athena built for Heracles against the sea monster, and they wrap themselves in cloud; the other side sit on the brows of Callicolone around Apollo and Ares. Both sides are loath to begin harsh war, though Zeus bids them from on high.

scenes.title: Achilles and Aeneas
scenes.summary: The plain fills with men and horses, and Achilles and Aeneas meet between the armies, Achilles coming on like a lion that men have wounded. He asks whether Aeneas hopes to win Priam's honor or a domain from the Trojans by killing him, and reminds him how he fled from the cattle on Ida to Lyrnessus. Aeneas answers that he too knows how to taunt, and tells his lineage: Zeus fathered Dardanus, who founded Dardania before Ilios was built in the plain; then came Erichthonius, whose mares the North Wind loved, so that their foals ran over the ripe grain and the breakers; Tros; Ilus, Assaracus and Ganymede, whom the gods snatched up to pour wine for Zeus; Laomedon and Priam on one side, Capys and Anchises on the other. It is Zeus who increases and diminishes the prowess of men; the tongue of mortals twists, and whatever word you speak, such will you hear back.

scenes.title: Poseidon Saves Aeneas
scenes.summary: Aeneas' spear drives through two layers of the shield of Hephaestus and is stopped in the gold; Achilles' spear passes through the rim of Aeneas' shield and over his back as he crouches. Achilles charges with his sword, and Aeneas lifts a stone that two men such as mortals are now could not carry. Poseidon grieves for the guiltless Aeneas: it is fated that he escape, so that the lineage of Dardanus may not perish, for Zeus has come to hate the lineage of Priam, and Aeneas and his children's children shall be lord over the Trojans. Hera leaves it to him, since she and Athena have sworn never to ward off the evil day from the Trojans. Poseidon sheds a mist over Achilles' eyes, sets his spear at his feet, and sends Aeneas flying over the ranks to the far edge of the war, warning him to draw back from Achilles until Achilles is dead. The mist lifts, and Achilles, amazed, lets Aeneas go and turns to the other Trojans.

scenes.title: Achilles and Hector Rally Their Men
scenes.summary: Achilles calls on the Achaeans to go man against man, since not even Ares or Athena could deal with so great a battle alone, and swears to go right through the Trojan ranks; Hector tells the Trojans he will go against Achilles even if his hands are like fire. Apollo warns Hector not to step out as a champion against Achilles, and Hector goes back into the crowd of men.

scenes.title: The First Men Achilles Kills
scenes.summary: Achilles kills Iphition, son of Otrynteus, born beneath Tmolus near the Gygaean lake, and boasts over him; Demoleon, son of Antenor, through the helmet; and Hippodamas, who bellows as he dies like a bull dragged around the Heliconian lord. Polydorus, Priam's youngest and dearest son, whom his father would not let fight, rushes through the champions to show off his speed and is struck through the back; he sinks down clutching his bowels.

scenes.title: Apollo Saves Hector
scenes.summary: When Hector sees Polydorus fall he comes against Achilles, and Achilles rejoices to meet the man who killed his companion. Hector answers that he knows Achilles is the better man, but these things lie on the knees of the gods. Athena blows Hector's spear back to his feet; Achilles charges, and Apollo hides Hector in thick mist. Three times Achilles strikes the mist, and the fourth time he says that Apollo has saved Hector again, but he will finish him off when he meets him later.

scenes.title: Achilles' Rampage
scenes.summary: Achilles kills Dryops, Demuchus, son of Philetor, Laogonus and Dardanus, the sons of Bias, and Tros, son of Alastor, who clasps his knees to beg for his life; then Mulius, Echeclus, son of Agenor, Deucalion, and Rhigmus from Thrace with his attendant Areithous. He rages like a fire through the glens of a parched mountain, and his horses trample corpses and shields like bulls treading out barley, until the axle and the rails of his chariot are spattered with blood and his hands with gore.

days.label: Day 27
days.note: The fourth day of battle, begun at 19.424, goes on: the gods join the war, Achilles meets Aeneas and Hector, and his killing begins; the day continues through Books 21 and 22.
